title: Kenyan Green Chilli Relish
community: Popular across Kenya — a fresh, herbal alternative to pili pili
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Green Chilli Relish — fresh green chillies, garlic, ginger, coriander, and lime blended into a vibrant, herbal, fiery green condiment. Fresher and more aromatic than standard pili pili — the green sauce that brightens everything it touches.
longDesc: Green chilli relish is the fresher, more herbal alternative to the tomato-based pili pili. The combination of fresh green chillies with coriander, ginger, and lime creates something that is simultaneously fiery and fragrant — the capsaicin heat of the chilli offset by the bright herbaceousness of the coriander. It is particularly good with grilled fish and coastal dishes.
steps: Dry-toast cumin seeds in a small pan for 30 seconds until fragrant. Cool.
Combine all ingredients in a blender.
Blend until smooth — or keep slightly coarse for texture.
Taste and adjust salt and lime.
chefTips: Toasting the cumin seeds first adds a deeper, nuttier flavour than raw cumin.
The oil helps emulsify the sauce and carries the fat-soluble flavour compounds.
For a milder version, remove chilli seeds before blending.
commonMistakes: Over-blending — loses the bright green colour as the chlorophyll breaks down from heat of motor.
Not enough salt — green sauces need generous seasoning.
cookingScience: The vibrant green colour of this relish comes from chlorophyll in the coriander and chilli. Extended blending generates heat from the blender motor that can break down chlorophyll — blend quickly and briefly to preserve the colour.
sustainabilityTips: Coriander and green chillies grow readily in Kenyan gardens.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 5 days. Freeze for 2 months.
healthBenefits: Green chillies contain more vitamin C than red chillies.
culturalNote: Green chilli relish represents the fresh, herbal dimension of Kenyan condiment culture — a brightness that complements rather than overpowers the richly spiced main dishes of the Kenyan table.
